markdown_report:
**Insights and directions.** SASRec supplies a strong sequential baseline. Preserve its score through a residual extension [1]. User feedback identifies stale interests outweighing repeated current interests. Recent recurrence therefore provides a useful conditioning signal. Electronics has 14.95% negative-over-positive rankings and a −0.4812 lower-decile margin. These training diagnostics motivate better discrimination, but do not establish validation gains.

Related work suggests three directions. Long/short preference models separate current intent from historical affinity [2]; their relevance here is selective history retrieval. gSASRec connects sampled BCE with overconfidence [3]; multi-negative objectives merit a controlled comparison. Candidate-conditioned attention retrieves history relevant to each candidate [4]; locally learned representations could support this without pretrained weights.

**Framework.** Organize interventions along two axes: *which evidence determines intent* (recent, recurrent, candidate-matched history) and *how candidates are separated* (BCE, multi-negative softmax). Semantic compatibility remains unknown when titles and descriptions omit specifications.

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives a positive reason and a limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform 32-negative softmax [3] | 2: useful adaptation; established | 7: scalable; sampling-sensitive | 4: sharper ranking; stale intent remains | 9: targets confusion; false negatives persist | 3: small loss change; exclusions require care |
| Recent recurrence attention residual [2,4] | 5: focused combination; familiar components | 8: interpretable intent retrieval; sparse-history limits | 9: addresses stale and loosely related choices; compatibility unproven | 7: candidate-specific separation; gains uncertain | 5: compact branch; candidate batching required |
| Scratch title/specification encoder [4] | 4: constraint-aware; standard pooling | 7: useful specificity; incomplete metadata | 8: direct content matching; overlap cannot prove fit | 6: may distinguish confusions; noisy semantics | 7: reusable encoder; token pipeline overhead |

**Selected: recent recurrence attention residual.** At 0% progress, test the second idea with the baseline objective first. It explicitly targets two reported failures: older occasional interests dominating current choices, and broadly related candidates outranking direct matches. Candidate-specific history evidence also targets the observed weak-margin tail, especially in Electronics.

For each causal prefix, compute attention between a candidate and historical item embeddings, adding bounded recency and recurrence biases. Pool the attended embeddings and add their candidate dot product to SASRec’s score through a learned scalar initialized to zero. Recurrence means repeated neighboring interests, estimated from training-only item co-occurrence; it does not imply repeat-item demand or unmet need.

Keep all four routed models, seeds, splits and artifact conventions. Update the predictor writer and diagnostic adapter together. Select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10; compare against baseline under equal GPU budgets. References describe motivations, not established benchmark gains.

idea.description: Add a candidate-conditioned attention residual over causal interaction history to each dataset-specific SASRec model, with bounded recency and recurring-interest biases.
idea.motivation: Address stale occasional interests and loosely related recommendations outranking direct current-interest matches. Improve candidate discrimination associated with Electronics’ observed weak-margin tail without treating embedding similarity near 0.5 as severe collapse.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, four-category routing, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Build sparse item co-occurrence statistics using training histories only; exclude self-links and cap neighbors. Compute recurrence support within each causal prefix, never from future interactions. Use bounded biases and a residual coefficient initialized to zero; retain the baseline loss initially to isolate the architecture change. Score candidates in chunks for full-catalog recommendations. Update the predictor writer to serialize and restore the attention branch, recurrence statistics, and scoring parameters. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Probe actual model scores through predict_score; if residual scoring requires history, carry causal context through log2feats without changing its public call signature. Return metrics and metric_definitions, identifying unavailable category breakdowns explicitly. Compare margins with the original sampling procedure and report added-branch ablations separately. Do not infer compatibility, satisfaction, or simulator traits from unavailable attributes. No executable baseline replacement can be specified reliably from the supplied architecture description alone; this is the requested research proposal and implementation pseudocode.
idea.pseudocode:
for each dataset and training batch:
    h = sasrec(causal_sequences)
    for each supervised causal prefix H and candidate c:
        E = item_embeddings(H)
        recurrence = bounded_neighbor_support(H, train_only_neighbors)
        logits = dot(E, query(c)) / sqrt(d)
        logits += bounded_recency_bias(H) + bounded_weight * recurrence
        attention = masked_softmax(logits, padding_mask(H))
        context = sum(attention * E)
        score[c] = dot(h, item_embedding(c))
        score[c] += tanh(residual_weight) * dot(context, item_embedding(c))
    optimize baseline_objective(score[positive], score[negative])
    # residual_weight starts at zero; gradients open the branch gradually
validate using pinned four-category macro HR@10
save all architecture parameters and update predictor writer

originality.positive: Combines candidate-specific history retrieval with explicit recent recurring-interest evidence under the unseen-item setting.
originality.negative: Attention, recency biases, recurrence features, and residual fusion are established components.

future_potential.positive: Provides a compact platform for studying which historical evidence supports specific current recommendations.
future_potential.negative: Sparse histories and unreliable co-occurrence neighborhoods may limit gains; no benchmark improvement has been measured.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses SASRec embeddings and introduces a small attention scoring branch.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires causal recurrence computation, chunked catalog scoring, predictor serialization, and diagnostic compatibility.

related_work.title: [1] Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses causal self-attention to represent sequential preferences and score candidate items.
limitations: The supplied baseline diagnostics show uneven discrimination across the four datasets; these are task-specific observations, not claims about every SASRec implementation.

related_work.title: [2] MSMT-LSI
contributions: The supplied search summary describes separate long- and short-term attention networks with temporal embeddings.
limitations: The supplied evidence does not establish improvements under the pinned RecHarness protocol.

related_work.title: [3] gSASRec extended abstract
contributions: Connects sampled BCE overconfidence with negative sampling and proposes generalized BCE with more negatives.
limitations: Does not establish that ordinary multi-negative softmax is optimal here or resolve historical-intent mismatch.

related_work.title: [4] Interaction Fidelity Attention
contributions: Motivates candidate-to-history attention and efficient processing of candidate interactions.
limitations: The proposed recency and recurrence residual is an adaptation, with no demonstrated gain on these four datasets.
